pages.title: Add a property
pages.description: Add a property by its name, before it has a loan, a T12 or any files.
pages.intro: A property needs only a name to start. Its profile, rent roll, T12, documents and loans can all come later. Before it makes the property, the app checks that you don’t have it already.

steps.text: Click **Specific Property** under the tabs.
Click **Add Property** in the bar. The **Add Property** window opens.

marks.label: Property name
marks.text: The property’s name: enough to start.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the window; nothing is made.

marks.label: Create
marks.text: Checks the name, then adds the property.

steps.text: Type the property’s name in **Property name**. Here it is the made-up “Birch Commons (example)”.
Click **Create**. The property joins the list in **Select a property**, marked “no loan yet”, and gets a folder of its own for its files.

marks.label: In the list
marks.text: Birch Commons (example) · no loan yet. Its page opens below the bar.

marks.label: Edit (greyed)
marks.text: **Edit**, **Remove** and **Refi Calculator** wait for a loan. The property’s page has its own **Archive**.

callouts.text: A name you already have, exactly, is refused with a short message.

sections.title: If the app asks first
sections.text: Before it makes a property, the app compares the name with your properties and loans.

steps.text: If the name looks like a property you have, click **Open it** when it is the same property, or **Create anyway** when it is a different one.

marks.label: Looks like
marks.text: The property, or properties, the name looks like.

marks.label: Open it
marks.text: It is the same property: open the one you have.

marks.label: Create anyway
marks.text: It is a different property: make it.

steps.text: If you archived a property with that name, click **Restore it** to bring it back with all its data, or **Start fresh** to make a new, empty one.

callouts.text: **Start fresh** deletes the archived property’s data for good. The app asks again before it does.

steps.text: If the name is one of your loans, or an address, click **Add a loan to it**. A new loan form opens on the property the name belongs to.
On the new property’s page, click **+ Add the first loan**. The loan form opens with the property’s name filled in.

marks.label: + Add the first loan
marks.text: Opens the loan form for this property.

steps.text: Fill in the loan and click **Save Loan**. See [Add a loan](add-a-loan).

next.text: Its units, its manager and its other facts.
Its units, occupancy and rents, from its rent roll.
Every part of a property’s page, named.

pages.title: Fill in a property’s profile
pages.description: Type in the property’s facts: its units, size, owner details, and an NOI to use before there is a T12.
pages.intro: The profile holds the property’s facts that don’t change often: its address, units, square feet, year built, acquisition date and manager. Claude’s stories and What to push use its units and address, with the T12, the rent roll and the loan agreement. Each field is saved as soon as you leave it.

steps.text: Click **Specific Property** under the tabs, and pick the property in **Select a property**.
Find **Property profile** on its page. On a property with no loan it is open already. On a property with a loan, click **Edit** in the bar at the top, or click the profile’s title.

marks.label: Property profile
marks.text: Click it to open or close the profile. Next to it: what is still missing.

steps.text: Type a value in a field, then leave it: press Tab, or click elsewhere. It is saved at once, with who changed it and when.
Fill in **Residential units**, **Acquisition date** and **Manager**. With these and the name, the profile is complete.

marks.label: Profile complete
marks.text: Every needed fact is in.

marks.label: Residential units
marks.text: Typed: 12.

marks.label: Last changed
marks.text: Who changed it, and when.

callouts.text: Units, square feet and year built are checked first: a number that can’t be right isn’t saved. A faded value is read from the property’s loan until you type your own.

sections.title: Enter an NOI before the T12
sections.text: A property with no T12 yet has no NOI. You can type one to use until its T12 is uploaded.

steps.text: Type the yearly NOI in **NOI (annual, entered)**, and leave the field. The NOI box uses it at once, and says so.

marks.label: Property NOI
marks.text: The NOI just typed.

marks.label: Your entered NOI
marks.text: Says the NOI is the one typed in the profile, with no T12 yet.

callouts.text: Once a T12 is uploaded, its NOI is used instead. See [Upload a T12](upload-a-t12).

steps.text: Type a yearly figure in **NOI override**, and leave the field. It replaces the T12’s NOI and the entered NOI on the property’s page, in the DSCR and the debt yield, and on the Portfolio page.

marks.label: Property NOI
marks.text: Now the override.

marks.label: Your NOI override
marks.text: Says the override is in use.

steps.text: To go back to the T12’s NOI, clear the field.

callouts.text: Only you can type an override. The refinance never uses a typed figure: it is sized on the T12, or on the underwriting approved from it.

steps.text: Click **history** next to a field’s name. The window lists every change: old and new value, who, when, and where it came from. Here **Residential units** was changed from 12 to 14.

marks.label: Old → new
marks.text: What it was and what it became.

marks.label: Who
marks.text: Who changed it.

marks.label: Where from
marks.text: Typed, a rent roll, the assistant, a loan agreement…

steps.text: Click **Close**.

next.text: Bring in its units and rents.
Every field of the profile, named.

pages.title: Import a rent roll
pages.description: Bring in a property’s rent roll to see its units, occupancy and rents.
pages.intro: Import the property’s rent roll to see its units, occupancy and average rents on its page. Underwriting fills in the units and the rent from it, and Claude’s stories and What to push use it with the T12.
before: The rent roll as a file: a Yardi export, an Excel workbook or a CSV. These pictures use a made-up rent roll of 12 units.

steps.text: On the property’s page, click **Import rent roll** in **Rent roll summary**.

marks.label: Rent roll summary
marks.text: Empty until a rent roll is imported.

marks.label: Import rent roll
marks.text: Opens your computer’s file window.

steps.text: Pick the rent roll in the window that opens. The app reads the file and lists its parts: one file can hold several properties.
Check the property set for each part. Opened from a property’s page, its part is set to that property.

marks.label: Use this part
marks.text: Ticked: this part is imported.

marks.label: Which property
marks.text: The property this part belongs to.

marks.label: Import
marks.text: Saves the file to the property’s folder.

steps.text: Click **Import**. The summary fills in on the property’s page.

marks.label: Units
marks.text: Residential units in the rent roll.

marks.label: Vacant
marks.text: Empty units.

marks.label: Update
marks.text: Brings in a newer rent roll.

callouts.text: Nothing is saved until you click **Import**. **Cancel** or **✕** closes the window without saving.

sections.title: Bring in a newer rent roll

steps.text: Click **Update** in **Rent roll summary**, and import the newer file the same way. It replaces the summary.

next.text: Every figure of the summary and the import window.

pages.title: The property page
pages.description: Every part of a property’s page: the bar, the NOI box, the profile, the rent roll summary, and the Add Property window.
pages.intro: Click **Specific Property** under the tabs and pick a property: its page opens below the bar. Each picture names its controls. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

sections.title: The property bar
sections.text: Under the tabs when **Specific Property** is on. The window bar and the tabs are on [The main screen](ref-main-screen).

marks.label: Whole Portfolio
marks.text: Back to the whole book.

marks.label: Specific Property
marks.text: One property at a time (on now).

marks.label: Select a property
marks.text: Pick a property; its page opens below. Next to a name: “senior + mezz” (two loans), “in a pooled loan” or “no loan yet”.

marks.label: Add Loan
marks.text: A new loan on this property. See [Add a loan](add-a-loan).

marks.label: Add Property
marks.text: A new property, by its name. See [Add a property](add-a-property).

marks.label: Edit
marks.text: Opens this property’s profile.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Archives this property and all its loans; it asks first. Bring it back from the Portfolio page’s Archived strip.

marks.label: Refi Calculator
marks.text: The refinance for this property. See [Run a refinance](run-a-refinance).

marks.label: The property’s page
marks.text: Starts here, under the bar.

marks.label: In the list
marks.text: “no loan yet” next to its name.

marks.label: Add Loan
marks.text: Its first loan.

marks.label: Add Property
marks.text: Another property.

marks.label: Edit (greyed)
marks.text: **Edit**, **Remove** and **Refi Calculator** are for a property with a loan. Its page has its own profile and **Archive**.

marks.label: Remove (greyed)
marks.text: Use **Archive** on the page instead.

marks.label: Refi Calculator (greyed)
marks.text: No loan to refinance yet.

views.text: From the top: the loan’s tiles and rate notice, the NOI box, the profile, the rent roll summary and the documents. Further down are the Loan Record and the payment schedule: see [A loan’s page](ref-loan-page).

marks.label: Tiles
marks.text: The loan’s main figures.

marks.label: Rate notice
marks.text: How a floating or hybrid rate is set this month.

marks.label: NOI box
marks.text: The property’s NOI, DSCR, debt yield and LTV, and where the NOI comes from.

marks.label: Property profile

marks.label: Build operating model
marks.text: Opens the property in Underwriting.

marks.label: Rent roll summary
marks.text: Units, occupancy and rents from its rent roll.

marks.label: Import rent roll
marks.text: Brings in its rent roll. See [Import a rent roll](import-a-rent-roll).

marks.label: Documents
marks.text: The property’s saved files. See [Documents and the T12 check](ref-documents).

marks.label: What you are adding
marks.text: The kind of file, or **Detect automatically**.

marks.label: Add files

sections.title: A property with no loan
sections.text: A new property, or one whose loans were all removed, has a page of its own. Removed or paid-off loans, if any, are listed on it with **Restore**.

views.title: The page
views.text: The profile opens by itself on this page; here it is closed to show the whole page.

marks.label: No loan yet
marks.text: Its name: the property has no active loan.

marks.label: + Add the first loan
marks.text: Opens a loan form with this property filled in.

marks.label: Archive
marks.text: Takes it out of the Portfolio page, the totals and the assistant. See [Archive or delete a property](archive-or-delete-a-property).

marks.label: NOI box
marks.text: Its NOI and value.

marks.label: Profile
marks.text: Its facts. Click to open or close.

marks.label: Rent roll summary
marks.text: Units, occupancy and rents from its rent roll.

marks.label: Import rent roll / Update

marks.label: Documents
marks.text: Its saved files. See [Documents and the T12 check](ref-documents).

marks.label: What you are adding
marks.text: The kind of file, or **Detect automatically**.

marks.label: Add files

views.title: Its NOI box

sections.title: The Add Property window and its questions

marks.label: Property name
marks.text: The property’s name: enough to start.

marks.label: Create
marks.text: Checks the name, then adds the property.

marks.label: Enter a property name
marks.text: **Create** with no name asks for one.

views.title: A similar name
views.text: A name that looks like one you have (here “Birch Commons”).

marks.label: Looks like
marks.text: The property, or properties, it looks like.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing is made.

marks.label: Create anyway

marks.label: Open it

views.text: A name you archived before (here the made-up “Old Mill (example)”).

marks.label: Already exists
marks.text: And when it was archived.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

marks.label: Start fresh
marks.text: Deletes the archived property’s data for good and makes a new, empty one. It asks again first.

marks.label: Restore it

views.text: A name that is one of your loans, or an address (here the sample “Avalon WP (Mezz)”), is not a new property.

marks.label: Cancel

marks.label: Add a loan to it

sections.title: Archived properties
sections.text: **Archive** on the page of a property with no loan, or **Remove** in the bar for a property with loans, takes it out of the Portfolio page, the totals and the assistant, and keeps everything. An archived property’s page shows **Un-archive** and **Delete permanently**, and the Portfolio page lists it in its **Archived** strip near the bottom. See [Archive or delete a property](archive-or-delete-a-property) for the pictures.

pages.title: Rename a property
pages.description: Change a property’s name, on every loan, file and list at once.
pages.intro: A property has one name, used everywhere. Change it in the property’s profile and the page, the property list and the Portfolio page all use the new name at once.

steps.text: Open the property’s profile: see [Fill in a property’s profile](fill-in-the-profile#open-the-profile).
Type the new name in **Property name**.
Leave the field: press Tab, or click elsewhere. The new name is saved, and the old one is kept in the field’s history.

marks.label: Property name
marks.text: The new name, saved.

marks.label: history (2)
marks.text: The old name and the new one.

marks.label: Address / market
marks.text: Changing it changes the address on all its loans.

callouts.text: On a property with loans, the name changes on every loan (a mezzanine loan keeps “(Mezz)”), and its files and chats move with it. If the new name already has files of its own, the app asks first: put them together, or don’t rename.

steps.text: Look at the top of the property’s page. The page, the property list and the Portfolio page all use the new name.

marks.label: The new name
marks.text: On its page, and in the property list.

marks.label: + Add the first loan
marks.text: A loan on the renamed property.

marks.label: Archive
marks.text: See [Archive or delete a property](archive-or-delete-a-property).

next.text: Take a property out of the book.

pages.title: Archive or delete a property
pages.description: Take a property out of the book and keep its data, bring it back, or delete it for good.
pages.intro: Archiving takes a property out of the Portfolio page, the totals and the assistant, and keeps all its data, ready to bring back. Deleting removes it for good. Only an archived property can be deleted.

steps.text: Open the property’s page.
Click **Archive** on its page. On a property with loans, click **Remove** in the bar at the top instead: it archives the property with all its loans. The app asks first.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: It leaves the Portfolio page, the totals and the assistant.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps it as it is.

marks.label: Archive
marks.text: Archives it.

steps.text: Click **Archive**. The page now says “archived”.

marks.label: archived
marks.text: Out of the Portfolio page, the totals and the assistant.

marks.label: Un-archive
marks.text: Brings it back, with all its data.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Removes it for good (it asks first).

steps.text: Click **Un-archive** on its page. It is back in the Portfolio page and the totals, with its profile, rent roll and files.

marks.label: Back
marks.text: No longer archived.

marks.label: Archive
marks.text: Archives it again.

steps.text: Or, on the Portfolio page, click the property’s name in the **Archived** strip near the bottom. The strip lists every archived property; here the made-up “Old Mill (example)”.

marks.label: Un-archive
marks.text: Click the name: it is back in the Portfolio page and the totals.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: The bin removes it and its files for good (it asks first).

steps.text: Archive the property, as above. Only an archived property can be deleted.
Click **Delete permanently** on its page. The window lists exactly what goes: its loans, T12, documents, chats, profile and figures.

marks.label: What goes
marks.text: Everything about the property, listed.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps it, archived.

marks.label: Delete permanently
marks.text: Deletes it for good.

steps.text: Click **Delete permanently**. The property is deleted, and you are back on the Portfolio page.

callouts.text: Deleting can’t be undone in the app. The automatic backups keep a copy: see [Back up and restore](back-up-and-restore). Portfolio conversations that mention the property are kept.

next.text: Bring back a removed loan or property from the Portfolio page.
